step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Nagra's forensic watermarking solution on AWS for both VOD and live content distribution. VOD processing begins in S3 where raw video is ingested, converted by AWS Elemental MediaConvert into A and B watermarked variants, and stored back in S3. Live video starts from an external camera feed into AWS Elemental MediaConnect, which passes it to AWS Elemental MediaLive to produce dual A/B watermarked channels, then to AWS Elemental MediaPackage for packaging. Both live and VOD channels feed into Amazon CloudFront. Player clients (Player 1, Player 2) request content through CloudFront, which triggers Lambda@Edge to select specific A/B segment sequences per session. Lambda@Edge queries Amazon DynamoDB to verify if the session is blacklisted. An external Nagra Detection Service (DS) extracts watermarks from pirated streams and populates blacklisted session tokens directly into DynamoDB to stop playout.

edges.notes: S3 supplies input video file to MediaConvert
MediaConvert uploads generated A/B watermarked variants back to S3
S3 serves as origin to CloudFront for VOD content
Live video stream input feeds into MediaConnect
MediaConnect routes live feed to dual MediaLive encoding channels
MediaLive sends A/B watermarked live streams to MediaPackage
MediaPackage serves live video stream origin to CloudFront
CloudFront triggers Lambda@Edge during request handling
Lambda@Edge queries DynamoDB to check session blacklisting status
CloudFront delivers personalized A/B video sequence to Player 1
CloudFront delivers distinct A/B video sequence to Player 2
Detection Service populates identified illicit session info into DynamoDB blacklist
